split_row.description: Split a line into a row span at `base`: the pipes, the cells, and each cell's content range. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes into the whole text, so `base` plus a position in the line.

cases.name: a compact row at a base
an escaped pipe does not split
an escaped backslash leaves the pipe a delimiter
a pipe in a code span still splits, as in GFM
whitespace after the closing pipe is no cell
text after the last pipe is a cell
an indented row at a base
a backslash before a multibyte character
a trailing backslash escapes the closing pipe
a no-break space is cell content

row_from_pipes.description: Build a row span from a line and the pipe offsets already found. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: uses the pipes it is given

row_pipes.description: The offsets of a line's unescaped pipes, read at `base`. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes.

is_delimiter_row.description: Whether a line is a delimiter row such as `| --- | :-: |`.

parse_align.description: The alignment a delimiter cell's spec gives: none, left, center or right.

cell_text.description: A cell's source read as text: its unescaped text and, for each position, the source offset. The offsets are given for ASCII source only; other source gives the text alone.

source_offset.description: The source offset of a position in a cell's text. ASCII source only.

text_offset.description: The text position of a source offset in a cell. ASCII source only.

escape_cell.description: Escape text for a table cell.

escape_cell_insert.description: Escape text typed into a cell: like `escape_cell`, with the rule for a backslash before the closing pipe.

escape_code_cell.description: Escape text for a cell inside a code span.

ends_with_escape.description: Whether a cell's source ends with an unpaired backslash escape.

literal_pipe_fixes.description: The edits that give a typed backslash before a pipe its pair. `inserted` holds ranges of the text in UTF-8 bytes; each fix is `{ from, to, insert }` in UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: a typed backslash before a pipe gets its pair
a deleted backslash takes its pair
a typed pipe after an odd run

row_cell_texts.description: The unescaped text of each cell in a line.

row_cell_sources.description: The source text of each cell in a line.

read_table.description: Read a table from its lines: the header, alignments, rows, and each cell's raw and unescaped text.

cases.name: an escaped pipe in a cell
ragged rows are kept as written
lines indented 4 spaces are no table
a delimiter narrower than the header
a second line that is no delimiter
a header with a CR left on it

table_grid.description: Read a table from its lines as a plain grid of cell text, with the issues found.

cases.name: an escaped pipe in a cell
ragged rows are kept as written

issues.message: 3 cells, header has 2; extra cells dropped

cases.name: lines indented 4 spaces are no table
a delimiter narrower than the header
a second line that is no delimiter
a header with a CR left on it

render_table.description: Render a header, rows and alignments as table lines. `line_break` sets what replaces a line break in a cell.

cases.name: short rows padded, long rows kept

pad_table.description: Pad a table's columns so its pipes line up. `max_column_width` caps a column's width; one that is not a positive integer is refused with `invalid_max_column_width`.

cases.name: a centered column, the odd space right
a skin-tone modifier joins its emoji

a cap wider than every cell

display_width.description: The display width of text in terminal columns.

row_line_text.description: The line for a row of cells, and the offset of each cell's content in it, in UTF-8 bytes.

insert_cell_splice.description: The splice that inserts a cell before column `at` of a line read at `base`: the change, the cursor anchor, and the offset. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: before a cell, after its opening pipe
a row without an opening pipe gets one
an indented opening pipe still opens the row
an unclosed row takes no trailing cell
past wide cells at a base

delete_cell_splice.description: The splice that deletes column `col` of a line read at `base`. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: the cell and the pipe after it
an unclosed last cell takes the pipe before it
an unclosed only cell keeps the opening pipe
a missing cell leaves the row alone

pad_row_splice.description: The splice that pads a row to `width` cells, or null when it has none to add. Offsets are UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: an unclosed row gets a closing pipe
an unclosed row ending in a space

has_trailing_pipe.description: Whether a line ends with a closing pipe.

table_lines.description: The lines of a table as `{ line, filler }`, where `line` is the index into `lines`. `delimiter` says whether line 1 is the delimiter row.

rectangular.description: Pad ragged rows with empty cells to the widest row's width.

pad_row.description: Pad one row of cells to `width` with empty cells.

clipboard_lines.description: Split clipboard text into lines, accepting LF, CRLF and CR.

grid_from_tsv.description: Read a grid from tab-separated text.

tsv_from_grid.description: Write a grid as tab-separated text. Tabs and line breaks in a cell become spaces.

to_csv.description: Write rows as CSV, quoting only what needs it.

grid_from_csv.description: Read a grid from CSV text.

grid_from_csv_paste.description: Read a grid from CSV text pasted from a clipboard, which is lenient about a trailing line break.

html_from_grid.description: Write a grid as an HTML table, with the shown text and the markdown source of each cell. `header` makes the first row header cells.

cases.name: a header row and escaped text

paste_rect.description: The rectangle a pasted grid covers from a `start` of `[row, col]`, or from a given `range`, and the value at each probe `[row, col]`; null when the rectangle covers no cell.

cases.name: a range is ignored for a larger grid
an empty first row covers nothing

round_trip.description: Write a grid in `format` (`tsv` or `csv`) and read it back.

sniff_delimiter.description: The delimiter a delimited text most likely uses.
